ink-ocean-regress-problem.title: The Great Inkwell
paragraphs: Narrator: At the source of the world was the Great Inkwell. Every belief anyone ever held was scooped from it.
Narrator: Beside it stood the guardian, a question mark. Bring it a ladle of ink and it asked you one question. Answer, and the ink dried into a stick you took home and fitted into yourself.
[A man holds up a ladle. A raven sits on his shoulder.]
Man: All ravens are black.
Question mark: Why?
Man: They're made of ink.
[The ink dries. He slots the stick into his chest, satisfied. The raven nods.]
Narrator: The guardian was not a strict examiner. Any answer would do.

ink-ocean-L4.title: Operation Because
paragraphs: Narrator: For the first time in its history, humanity united. It elected the three greatest minds alive and gave each of them unlimited ink, unlimited time and absolute authority.
Narrator: Each was given one task: answer it.

ink-ocean-regress-skepticism.title: Pyrrho, the Unmoved
paragraphs: SKEPTICISM. None of our beliefs is justified, so suspend judgment on everything. (Unit 1.1)
Y: Why believe anything?
Pyrrho: I don’t. No more this than that.
[Beside him, his old teacher Anaxarchus is sinking into the wet ink, waving.]
Narrator: His teacher fell into a bog. Pyrrho walked right past. He had suspended judgment on the bog.
Narrator: His teacher later praised him for it. This really happened.
The objection — you can’t live by it; acting at all takes believing something.

ink-ocean-regress-infinitism.title: Peirce, the Endless
paragraphs: INFINITISM. The chain of reasons never stops: B1 rests on B2, B2 on B3, and so on, forever. (Agrippa’s mode of infinite regress, Unit 1.1)
Y: Why believe that?
Peirce: Because of B2.
Y: And B2?
Peirce: B3. There is no first reason. Every thought rests on an earlier one.
[The camera tilts down. He’s standing on a turtle, standing on a turtle, standing on a turtle, out of frame.]
Narrator: Turtles all the way down. He was last seen still descending.
The objection — at any finite time, the justification is still unfinished (Unit 1.1). Nothing ever dries.

ink-ocean-regress-coherentism.title: Neurath, the Shipwright
paragraphs: COHERENTISM. A belief is justified if it belongs to a coherent system of beliefs: a web, not an edifice. (Agrippa’s mode of circularity, Unit 1.2)
Y: Why believe the ship is sound?
Neurath: Because every plank holds.
Y: Why believe every plank holds?
Neurath: Because the ship is sound.
Y: That's a circle.
Neurath: It's a web. No belief stands alone; each is held up by all the others. The bigger the circle, the better.
[SOWATT swims laps around the ship, looking for a loose end. There isn't one.]
SOWHAT: So what? A fairy tale can fit together perfectly too.
Narrator: It was the most coherent ship in history. Not one plank contradicted another. It sailed, perfectly consistent, off the edge of the map.
The objection — the isolation problem. A perfectly coherent system can be cut off from experience, so coherence alone isn’t enough (Unit 1.2).
